title: What is the reciprocal of the divisor?
text: Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal: flip the second fraction, then multiply. The reciprocal of $$\frac{2}{5}$$ is $$\frac{5}{2}$$. A common mistake is to flip the first fraction, or to divide the numerators and denominators separately. After rewriting, the problem is $$\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{5}{2}$$. What is the numerator of that product, before simplifying?

title: Denominator of the product
text: What is $$4 \times 2$$, the denominator before simplifying?

title: Worked solution
text: $$\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{5}{2} = \frac{15}{8}$$. $$\frac{15}{8}$$ is already in lowest terms. Common mistake: flipping $$\frac{3}{4}$$ instead of $$\frac{2}{5}$$, or answering $$\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2}{5}$$. General rule: keep the first fraction, flip the second, and change division to multiplication.
